label: Hunter Biden Laptop Story Spreads
detail: Reporting on the contents of the son's laptop reaches far more voters before election day, through major outlets and social media.
assumption: Wider exposure to the laptop story lowers favourable views of the challenger among some persuadable and low-attention voters, mostly those who are not strongly partisan. Strong partisans and early voters are barely affected.
facts_text: Major newspapers, television networks and social media platforms have carried the story widely in the final weeks of the campaign, and it is among the most discussed items of the week.
nominee_news: Newspapers and broadcasters have given prominent, sustained coverage to emails said to come from a laptop belonging to his son, which allege that the son arranged introductions to his father with a foreign energy company.
He has denied any wrongdoing and says he never discussed his son's business dealings with him.
research_questions: How much did late-campaign scandal stories change the vote choice of undecided voters in past presidential elections?
How did voters who had already cast early ballots respond to late-breaking news in earlier elections?
How have voters reacted to allegations about a candidate's family members in past campaigns?
How did the reach of major media outlets versus social media shape what voters knew in the final week of a campaign?
source_text: the hunter biden laptop story was more widely circulated
